ATLAS
The $1 billion industrial gas platform

An AI deal desk that finds, researches, values and sequences acquisitions for a private equity buy-and-build, from a 703-company map to a plan to $1bn revenue.

Ade Thiruchandran · Repo (public): https://github.com/adethiru/cylinder-atlas

The problem

Building a $1bn roll-up starts with a list nobody has

  • Who: a PE investor (me: ex-Crescent, Ardian, Shore Capital) building a buy-and-build in industrial gas distribution
  • Why this sector: recurring cylinder rental, defensive end markets, about 1,000 fragmented US independents, and a proven model (Meritus Gas Partners)
  • Today: an external due diligence provider takes 2–3 weeks per deal list, then spreadsheets for valuation and sequencing
  • Cost of delay: rival roll-ups (Meritus, AWG, Arc3, Holston, Airgas) are calling the same family owners

How the agents work

Code for maths, four agents for judgement

All agents use gpt-6-luna (course key). The Scout is the only tool-using agent. The shared ~3k-token thesis prefix is cached.

Demo · one real run

Lampton Welding Supply, run #43: 5 facts verified, $0.0025

Trace → verified quotes (from the GAWDA Media fallback, because the company's site was unreachable) → 7 risks, each with a mitigation. Red Ball's site blocked the Scout, so it reported "unknown", not guesses.

Demo · from list to plan

30 deals to $1.00bn · 39% gross IRR · 5.1x MOIC

Platform = Red Ball Oxygen, sized for a first cheque. The Strategist phases the roll-up and flags a route-density risk. Base-case screening assumptions; 69% of the gain is multiple arbitrage.

40 deal desks + 8 Strategist runs per user per month. Whole project: 236 calls, $0.0635.

Cost levers: cached thesis prefix (−58%), code instead of LLM for ranking and maths, step, page and $ caps.

Experiment: cutting pages from 6k to 2k characters saved 20–28% but lost 60–83% of verified facts, so I kept 6k.

Safety · shown working

A booby-trapped website could not hijack the agents

  • Injection filter: 5 hidden instructions removed (run #51)
  • Domain allow-list: blocks other sites, IPs, localhost, file://
  • Quote verifier: 13 invented facts rejected
  • Budget kill-switch: $ and token caps checked before every call
  • Step limits: 8 loop stops logged
  • Human approval: no email capability
  • Keys: redacted, never in the browser

5/5 guard tests pass offline.

What's next

Limits and the next month

Limits today

  • Some websites block automated readers
  • Financials estimated until a CIM is entered
  • UK and Europe coverage thinner than North America
  • Single user, local; returns are a screening model

Next

  • Registry and PHMSA/OSHA data, licensed feeds via CSV
  • Deal-by-deal timing, bear/base/bull returns
  • Hosted team workspace with login
  • Pilot with 3–5 PE users: time, quality, owner conversations
